chief_complaint: left calf swelling, warmth, and throbbing pain after knee surgery
hpi_details: A 47-year-old male presents to the clinic with left calf swelling, warmth, and throbbing pain after knee surgery. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks his calf pain and swelling are just a severe muscle strain from pushing too hard in physical therapy.
concerns: He is worried that an infection has spread into his new knee joint and will require another operation.
expectations: He hopes to get an ultrasound to make sure the joint is intact and a temporary prescription for anti-swelling medication.

investigation_events.title: Compression ultrasound of the left leg
investigation_events.availability_message: The left-leg compression ultrasound report is now available.

results.value: Non-compressible left popliteal vein with intraluminal thrombus extending into the distal femoral vein
results.reference_range: Veins fully compressible with normal flow

clinical_knowledge.topic: Deep Vein Thrombosis evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Deep Vein Thrombosis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Deep Vein Thrombosis: Order compression ultrasound, start therapeutic anticoagulation for 3 months, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: left calf swelling, warmth, and throbbing pain after knee surgery

Key HPI features: A 47-year-old male presents to the clinic with left calf swelling, warmth, and throbbing pain after knee surgery. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Deep Vein Thrombosis.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Deep Vein Thrombosis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cellulitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Chest pain, breathlessness, or coughing blood — pulmonary embolism.
management_principles: Plan for Deep Vein Thrombosis: Order compression ultrasound, start therapeutic anticoagulation for 3 months
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Deep Vein Thrombosis.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Deep Vein Thrombosis.
reference_soap.plan: Plan for Deep Vein Thrombosis: Order compression ultrasound, start therapeutic anticoagulation for 3 months. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

teaching.one_liner: A clot in a deep leg vein: unilateral swelling, warmth and calf tenderness. The reason it matters is the lung it can travel to.
red_flags: Chest pain, breathlessness, or coughing blood — pulmonary embolism

must_ask.say: Is it just the one leg, or both?
Have you had a long flight, an operation, or been off your feet recently?
Have you had cancer, or a clot before?
Are you on testosterone therapy, or do you have any condition that makes your blood clot more easily?
Have you had any chest pain or shortness of breath?
When did it start, and how long does it last each time?

history.answer: My left calf has been swollen, warm, and throbbing with pain after my knee surgery.
The swelling is only in my left calf and lower leg; my right leg, face, and belly look completely normal.
It started about three days ago and has been gradually getting more swollen and painful each day.
No, it stays swollen and throbbing all day and night without going down in the morning.
Yes, when I press my finger on my left shin or take my sock off, it leaves a noticeable indentation.
No, my body weight has stayed the same over the past few weeks.
Yes, my left calf has a constant throbbing ache, feels hot to the touch, and looks slightly pinkish.
No, I have not had any shortness of breath, and I can lie flat comfortably at night.
No, I don't have any chest pain, and I haven't coughed up any blood.
My urine looks clear and normal, with no bubbles, blood, or change in how much I produce.
No, my abdomen is not bloated, my eyes and skin are not yellow, and I haven't noticed easy bruising.
No, I haven't had a sore throat, runny nose, or skin cut recently.
I have felt unusually tired over the last few days, but I don't feel sensitive to the cold and my skin isn't dry.
My appetite has been normal, I have had no diarrhea, and I haven't lost weight.
I had arthroscopic surgery on my left knee two weeks ago and have stayed mostly resting on the couch since then.
No, I have never had a blood clot before, and I don't have cancer.
I took some prescribed pain relievers for the first three days after surgery, but I am not taking any medications now.
No, I have never had hepatitis or liver problems, and I rarely drink alcohol.
No, I have never been diagnosed with high blood pressure, diabetes, or heart disease.
I eat normal home-cooked meals without extra salt, and I haven't been on any long car or airplane trips.
I figured my calf was just swollen and sore because my physical therapist pushed me too hard yesterday.
I'm really worried that my surgical site got infected and they'll have to reopen my knee to fix it.
I'm hoping to get an ultrasound to make sure everything is healing right and something to bring down the swelling.
I have always been healthy and have no chronic medical conditions.
Aside from the left knee arthroscopy two weeks ago, I have never had surgery or stayed in the hospital.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter pills, or health supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink socially, maybe a beer or two once or twice a month.
I work as an office manager and live with my wife and son in an apartment.
There is no family history of blood clots, clotting disorders, heart disease, or kidney failure.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 125/80 mmHg, pulse 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Left calf is noticeably swollen with circumference 3.5 cm greater than the right, warm to touch, and tender to deep palpation.
Two-plus pitting edema noted over the left lower leg and medial malleolus; no edema on the right leg.
Healing surgical incision over the left anterior knee without effusion, with left calf pain elicited upon passive ankle dorsiflexion.
Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are palpable and symmetric bilaterally.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without crackles, wheezes, or pleural friction rubs.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal first and second heart sounds; no murmurs, gallops, or third heart sound.
Jugular venous pulsation is not elevated and there is no jugular venous distension.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender with no hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, or shifting dullness.
Conjunctivae are normal pink and sclerae are non-icteric without periorbital edema.
Erythema and warmth confined to the left calf without skin breakdown, petechiae, or spider angiomas.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and smooth with no nodules or thrills.
